weekend_substitution_rule.statement: Irish law gives no automatic substitute weekday when a fixed-date public holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday. The employee's entitlement is discharged by paid time off, an extra annual-leave day or extra pay, but the following Monday does not itself become a public holiday.
weekend_substitution_rule.consequence_for_deadlines: Saint Stephen's Day 2026-12-26 falls on a Saturday and Monday 2026-12-28 is NOT a public holiday in IE. A MDCG 2023-3 roll-forward therefore lands on 2026-12-28, not 2026-12-29.

caveats: Good Friday is NOT a public holiday in the Republic of Ireland, despite being widely observed and despite being one in several neighbouring jurisdictions. It is deliberately absent from this file.
Easter Sunday is not a public holiday in IE either; only Easter Monday is.

No entry in this file was fetched from gov.ie directly — gov.ie and citizensinformation.ie both refused automated fetches. Every date below was confirmed against at least two independent listings AND is reproducible from the statutory moveable-feast rule stated in its `basis` field. The `tools/clock` test suite re-derives each moveable date from that rule.
